sources.entry: How To Remember Anything Forever-ish: a comic about learning

summary.title: How To Remember Anything Forever-ish
summary.one_liner: Spaced repetition works by spacing out recall with increasing gaps, and this interactive comic teaches the science and practice of it through games and flashcard demos.
keywords: how to remember things long term
takeaways: Spaced repetition combines testing (active recall) with time, using increasing gaps between reviews.
Common practices like lectures, cramming, and re-reading are described as ineffective for long-term retention.
The Leitner Box moves a card up one level when you get it right and back to level 1 when wrong, doubling the review gap per level.
Good flashcards are small, connected, and meaningful, per the comic's advice.
summary.summary: An interactive comic by Nicky Case, about the art and science of remembering things. It walks through the forgetting curve (with and without recall), explains spaced repetition as testing plus time, and demonstrates the Leitner Box system with playable simulations. A worked example uses mitochondria flashcards to show how to write good cards. It ends with downloadable resources and a further reading list covering books and studies on spaced repetition and learning methods.
